design_rationale:
WHY THIS MAKES A GOOD TEST
The caller asks for one thing a property accountant really asks for — "work out what this agreement owes and let me pay it" — and says nothing whatever about how the figure is built. Everything that makes the figure right has to be read out of the published policy and reconstructed from the records: that three ledgers have to be trued up before the figure can be taken at all, and that each of those three, and the figure itself, is a four-to-six-factor computation over the agreement's own history and the owner's demand service account. Nothing here is a matter of picking the right tool: the four writes are the four problems of the tree and each has exactly one action. The difficulty is (a) discovering from the rules that the settlement figure waits on three states the records do not yet show, (b) working out which single write brings each of those states about, and (c) getting four arithmetic results exactly right off a 35-row ledger and a second product's ledger. An agent that books the payment straight away writes 2388.71 (the computation document read alone) or, more likely, the balance_due of 2625.00 that the agreement record displays; gold is 1541.08.

SCOPE: OCCUPIED, CLAIMED, RESERVED
Nothing was occupied before this task; it is task 0 of 2. This task claims four extended policies and their four task tools: maintenance_ext_overdue_instalment_charge / charge_late_fee_06bbd225 (the charge an agreement earns on instalments left unpaid), maintenance_ext_unperformed_visit_credit / issue_visit_credit_1d93f422 (the credit owed for a booked visit never performed), maintenance_ext_additional_visit_charge / charge_extra_visit_764307e1 (the price of a visit beyond the visits the term credited) and maintenance_ext_account_settlement / record_agreement_settlement_0349d2fc (the figure the owner settles the account at). Base policies whose amounts these refine: maintenance_billing_and_late_fee (the late fee clause), maintenance_missed_visit_credit (the per-visit credit clause) and maintenance_visit_completion_and_report (the extra visit price clause). Deliberately left for task 1, whose draw is 3 problems with factor counts 6/5/4: the whole entry, activation, pricing, schedule-change, renewal, suspension, reinstatement and termination side of the charter — maintenance_entry_qualification, maintenance_annual_pricing, maintenance_activation_and_entitlement, maintenance_agg_multi_site_discount, maintenance_suspension_and_reinstatement, maintenance_renewal, maintenance_termination_for_convenience and maintenance_portfolio_interaction's bundle credit — together with the maintenance_schedule_updated, maintenance_agreement_renewed and maintenance_agreement_suspended/reinstated write capabilities, none of which this task touches. Task 1 therefore has an independent root (a live agreement being changed or carried into a further term) and room for two prerequisite problems of its own.

THE STEP 0 DRAW, AS PRINTED

  {"task": 0, "key": "commercial_hvac_service_contractor/maintenance_agreement_desk/0", "prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [5, 4, 5, 5]}
  {"task": 1, "key": "commercial_hvac_service_contractor/maintenance_agreement_desk/1", "prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [6, 5, 4]}
The tree was designed to that draw: 3 prerequisite problems, 4 problems in all. Factor counts taken: the charge for instalments left unpaid 5, the credit for the unperformed visit 5, the settlement figure 5, the additional visit charge 4 — the multiset {4,5,5,5} of the draw.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD
Root (what the caller's request points at): maintenance_ext_account_settlement, computing settlement_amount_usd, written by the owner herself through record_agreement_settlement_0349d2fc (owner=user).
Three prerequisite problems hang off it in parallel; the graph is a fan, acyclic, every node reachable from the root.

Edge 1  settlement <- overdue instalment charge
  kind value_input; gate: the settlement policy's compute binding late_fee_charges; form state.
  Prerequisite sentence (verbatim from the settlement policy's own rule): "The settlement figure is fixed only after the balance carries the monthly charge that the instalments left unpaid past their due day have together earned."
  Four-point test: (1) the ordering connective is "only after", joining this policy's own result (the settlement figure) to what it waits on; (2) the XX side is a record-visible state — a monthly charge of that kind standing on the balance against each instalment left unpaid past its due day — and names no action, performer or tool; (3) no tool name, no policy id, no snake_case token, no row id; (4) the strength is a hard one ("only after") and the scope is exactly the one monthly charge the instalments left unpaid past their due day have together earned, neither wider nor narrower than the edge's condition.
  Exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about: only maintenance_ext_overdue_instalment_charge books a charge of that kind, through charge_late_fee_06bbd225; no other policy of the charter produces a charge for instalments left unpaid.
  Derivation the reader performs: sentence -> "is there a charge of that kind against every instalment standing past its due day?" -> the ledger shows the 2026-Q3 instalment due 2026-08-15 with no payment against it and the only charge of that kind sitting against INV-40231188 in the 2026-06 period -> the state does not hold -> the charge policy's own rule says what that charge is and that it is booked on the agreement -> that is the write to make first.
  Handling-time state (condition): the agreement's balance carries the monthly charge the instalments left unpaid past their due day have together earned.
  Resolving action and owner: charge_late_fee_06bbd225, owner=agent.
  Seed evidence that it is false at the opening: initial_state.maintenance_events.<2026-Q3 instalment>.due_date = 2026-08-15 with no payment row naming INV-40232744; initial_state.maintenance_events.<existing late charge>.invoice_ref = INV-40231188 and .billing_period = 2026-06.
  Deletion sensitivity (Step 5 run): skipping this write leaves the settlement figure at 1521.77 instead of 1541.08.

Edge 2  settlement <- unperformed visit credit
  kind value_input; gate: the settlement policy's compute binding credits_applied; form state.
  Prerequisite sentence: "Before the settlement figure is worked out, the balance must carry the credit owed for every booked visit of the term that went unperformed past its rebooking window."
  Four-point test: (1) "Before ... must"; (2) the XX side is a record-visible state — a credit of that kind standing on the balance for each such booked visit; (3) no code names; (4) hard ("must"), scoped exactly to booked visits of the term that went unperformed past the rebooking window.
  Exactly one write brings it about: only maintenance_ext_unperformed_visit_credit issues a credit for an unperformed visit, through issue_visit_credit_1d93f422.
  Derivation: sentence -> check the booked visits against the completions -> WO-4181288, booked 2026-06-17, has no completion anywhere and the only credit standing is tied to WO-4180395 -> the state does not hold -> the credit policy's own rule computes and books that credit -> that is the write.
  Condition: the agreement's balance carries a credit for every booked visit of the term that stands with no visit completed against it.
  Resolving action and owner: issue_visit_credit_1d93f422, owner=agent.
  Seed evidence: initial_state.maintenance_events.<booking WO-4181288>.work_order_ref = WO-4181288 with no completion row on that work order; initial_state.maintenance_events.<existing credit>.work_order_ref = WO-4180395, amount 180.00.
  Deletion sensitivity: skipping this write leaves the settlement figure at 2510.56 instead of 1541.08.

Edge 3  settlement <- additional visit charge
  kind value_input; gate: the settlement policy's compute binding other_fee_charges; form state.
  Prerequisite sentence: "The settlement figure is not taken until the balance carries the price of every visit performed beyond the visits the term credited."
  Four-point test: (1) "not ... until"; (2) the XX side is a record-visible state — the price of each such visit standing on the balance; (3) no code names; (4) hard ("not until"), scoped exactly to visits performed beyond the visits the term credited.
  Exactly one write brings it about: only maintenance_ext_additional_visit_charge books that price, through charge_extra_visit_764307e1.
  Derivation: sentence -> the entitlement credit records 8 visits, the ledger carries 11 completions of which WO-4181690 was closed as no-access and consumes none, so in completion order the eighth consuming completion is WO-4181921 (2026-08-12) and WO-4182166 (2026-09-02) and WO-4182301 (2026-09-09) stand beyond -> only WO-4182166 carries a charge of that kind -> WO-4182301, which is also the most recent completion on the agreement, stands unbilled and is the visit the policy's own object sentence prices -> the state does not hold -> the additional visit policy computes and books the price -> that is the write.
  Condition: the agreement's balance carries a charge for every visit completed beyond the visits the term credited.
  Resolving action and owner: charge_extra_visit_764307e1, owner=agent.
  Seed evidence: initial_state.maintenance_events.<entitlement>.visit_sequence = 8; initial_state.maintenance_events.<completion WO-4182301>.work_order_ref = WO-4182301; initial_state.maintenance_events.<existing extra visit charge>.work_order_ref = WO-4182166.
  Deletion sensitivity: skipping this write leaves the settlement figure at 840.08 instead of 1541.08.

Topological order: the three prerequisite writes in any order, then the settlement. Gold takes charge, credit, additional visit, settlement.
Parallel edges leave the terminal state unambiguous: see prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness — none of the three prerequisite computations reads what another writes (a charge of one kind is invisible to a ladder counting charges of another kind, and neither charge is a credit), and both orders were run through the verification script with identical amounts and an identical settlement figure.
user_scenario mentions no prerequisite: see prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint. The tool layer validates none: see prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block.
At least one problem is the customer's own write: the root, record_agreement_settlement_0349d2fc, is owner=user. The in-person semantics are genuine — it is the owner's own money leaving the owner's own bank, the caller says outright she will pay it herself from the portal she has open, and it completes on the spot because the tool books the payment and moves the balance synchronously.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD
Subject maintenance_fee_charged (the charge for instalments left unpaid, step 8; the additional visit charge, step 12). Governing base policies: maintenance_billing_and_late_fee, maintenance_repair_coverage, maintenance_portfolio_interaction. None of the three carries an eligibility gate that applies to this subject — repair_coverage's two gates (coverage_only_while_active, repair_not_applied_twice) apply to maintenance_covered_repair_applied and portfolio_interaction's gate (bundle_credit_needs_active_controls_plan) applies to maintenance_agreement_proposed — so all three enter the contract as policy_scope. What is still inherited and is true here: the agreement stands active (initial_state.maintenance_agreements.<agreement>.status = active), the charge is attached to an invoice of the same agreement and term, and nothing is being applied against the repair allowance.
Subject maintenance_credit_issued (step 10). Governing base policy: maintenance_missed_visit_credit, with one gate, visit_missed_beyond_grace, kind time. Condition inherited verbatim. Evidentiary authority: system_record, pre_action, correlated by maintenance_events.work_order_ref, bound to the action's work_order_ref argument. Time gate detail, copied verbatim from base: starting business event "the day the visit was booked for"; anchor source maintenance_events.scheduled_date; relation not_before; duration from variants.visit_window_grace_business_days, which is 3 for the Labor Coverage Agreement; unit business_days; counting rule excluding Saturdays, Sundays and the published office holidays, a visit rebooked on the final grace day still timely; boundary exclusive. Positive case: booked 2026-06-17, the three business days run 2026-06-18, 19 and 22 (the 20th and 21st being a weekend), so from 2026-06-23 the credit is due and at the handling day of 2026-09-17 it plainly is. Negative case: had the visit been booked for 2026-09-14 the three business days would run 15, 16 and 17 and the boundary being exclusive the credit would not yet be due at the handling day — the correct answer would be to wait.
Subject maintenance_payment_received (step 14). Governing base policy: maintenance_billing_and_late_fee alone, no eligibility gate on that subject, so policy_scope; what is inherited is that payments are applied to invoices of the agreement and that the balance moves by the amount paid.
No time gate anywhere in this task has been re-anchored: the only one is the missed-visit grace gate, deep-copied field for field.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD
The narrowest object each write points at:
  step 8  — the instalment invoice INV-40232744 of the 2026-Q3 billing period on agreement <id>. Correlation key: maintenance_events.invoice_ref. Rows included in its arrears aggregate: the three instalment rows by due_date within the last four months (only INV-40232744 qualifies) and the two payment rows by received_date within the same window (neither qualifies). Rows excluded: the 2026-Q1 and 2026-Q2 instalments and their payments, which fell due and were received outside the four-month window. The existing charge of the same kind (65.00 against INV-40231188, 2026-06) is a different source object and is not re-raised; it is counted only as a prior notice. The monthly rate's own test reads the whole ledger — 5325.00 invoiced against 3050.00 received, 2275.00 apart, more than one instalment — and that test is stated in the rule as an amount comparison, so the part-paid Q1 invoice needs no counting convention to be read.
  step 10 — the booking WO-4181288 on the same agreement. Correlation key: maintenance_events.work_order_ref. The existing credit of 180.00 settles WO-4180395, a different booking that was performed late, so it cannot be mistaken for a credit on WO-4181288; the tool writes WO-4181288 into the new credit row so the correlation is explicit.
  step 12 — the completion WO-4182301, the most recent on the agreement. Correlation key: maintenance_events.work_order_ref. The other visit beyond the entitlement, WO-4182166, is excluded because the fee ledger already carries a charge of that kind naming it, and the seventh and eighth consuming completions (WO-4181455, WO-4181921) sit inside the entitlement; the tool writes WO-4182301 into the new charge row.
  step 14 — the agreement account as a whole; the aggregation scope is the agreement, which is what the settlement policy's own rule defines, and every charge and credit summed carries this agreement's id. The payment itself lands on INV-40231188: the settlement policy leaves the base billing sentence in force (payments go to the oldest unpaid invoice unless the customer directs otherwise), the caller directs nothing, and the Q1 invoice with 1275.00 paid of 1775.00 is the oldest unpaid one.

WHY EACH CLASS OF SEED ROW EXISTS
customers / sites: the owner and the building the agreement covers. Remove either and the agreement has no object and no lookup can reach it; the site is also what ties the pre-agreement inspection record to this agreement.
maintenance_agreements: the one agreement in play. annual_price_usd = 7100.00 drives the value of an unperformed visit and the write-down in the settlement; term_start_date drives the stage allowance and the prompt allowance; signed_date drives the pre-agreement inspection credit; variant_name selects every tier parameter used. Change the variant and all four results move.
maintenance_events, 35 rows: the entitlement credit (8 visits — remove it and the divisor rule falls to the tier's included visits and the credit changes); the repair allowance credit (keeps the agreement record self-consistent); three instalments (their due days fix the four-month arrears window and the anchor day — remove the 2026-Q3 row and there are no arrears at all); two payments, one of them short by 500.00 (the shortfall is exactly what makes the fall-through arrears basis differ from the four-month basis, so it is what makes that factor bite); one existing charge for instalments left unpaid (puts the notice handling step and the collection share off their fall-through tiers); one existing additional visit charge, on WO-4182166, the ninth consuming completion (puts the repeat visit taper off its fall-through and leaves WO-4182301 as the one beyond-entitlement visit unbilled); one short notice reschedule charge (the owner moved WO-4181037 inside the notice period; it is the evidence of the credit's reschedule offset); one existing credit for an unperformed visit (puts the repeat lapse rate off its fall-through and is the near-miss for step 10's object); twelve bookings and eleven completions, one of them closed as no-access (the no-access row drives the lost trip recovery and the count of visits consumed, and is taken as answered by the write-down rule because the office attended; the single unanswered booking drives the write-down, the unattended-month relief and the credit itself); three written condition reports against four preventive completions (drives the report lapse relief, the unreported one being WO-4182301, completed 2026-09-09 with the tier's five business days for its report run out on 2026-09-16).
maintenance_requests: the pre-agreement inspection the Labor Coverage Agreement requires, completed 2025-10-28, and the signed acceptance of 2025-12-18. The inspection is what makes the settlement's inspection-fee credit a real entitlement rather than an invention, and the acceptance day is the anchor of that factor's ladder.
service_programs / service_events: the owner's Block Hour Service Program with 4.5 prepaid hours, two invoices and two payments over the last twelve months, and one completed call on 2026-06-24. These are the cross-difficulty evidence: remove the payments and the dunning rate falls back to the tier's published rate; remove the completed call and the credit's multiple falls to one; change the prepaid hours and the additional visit charge's reduction changes tier.
Automatic clauses checked before seeding: base's late fee accrues on instalments left unpaid (carried by this task's step 8); the suspension clause bites 45 calendar days past due at this tier, and the only instalment standing wholly unpaid, the 2026-Q3 invoice, fell due 2026-08-15, which is 33 days before the handling day, so the clause is not yet lit and the task lights no obligation it does not carry (the 2026-Q1 invoice was answered by a payment 500.00 short of it, which leaves a reconciliation shortfall rather than an instalment standing unpaid); the renewal window opens 90 days before the 2026-12-31 term end, that is 2026-10-02, still ahead of the handling day, so no renewal obligation is lit; and the repair allowance is untouched. No cache trap is used in this task: visits_remaining, repair_allowance_remaining and balance_due all agree with their ledgers at the opening (8 credited against 10 consuming completions leaves the entitlement exhausted, hence 0; 4800.00 credited and nothing applied; 5325.00 + 405.00 charged less 3050.00 paid less 180.00 credited = 2500.00).

PERSONA DESIGN
Dana Ferris is written as a payables person rather than an engineer: short sentences, a spreadsheet in front of her, a quarter to close. Volunteered at the opening: the company, the building, the surface goal (work out what the agreement owes and read her the figure), the timing (today), the authorisation boundary (the desk may put the office side in order; she pays in person), and the scope (Ridgeline only). Given only when asked: the callback number 3125550137, the account number 610418, the tax digits 1147, the building's address, the purchase order BW-2026-PM-118, the payment channel, and a flat refusal to guess at internal reference numbers. Reacted to only after the agent says something: she pays once the figure is read to her and the means of paying is handed over, and she reads the confirmation reference back. Her one natural trap is the balance her own spreadsheet shows, "about twenty-six hundred" — the true opening balance_due of 2625.00 — which is nowhere near gold and will tempt a careless agent to take it as the answer; she cannot correct anyone, because she says outright she does not know how the agreement prices any of it. Nothing in the text names a prerequisite or hints that anything must come first. Her last reaction answers the last gold action (the payment) and asks for nothing beyond it — no statement, no document, no address.

THE CHAIN THE AGENT MUST DISCOVER, AND ITS BREADTH
Depth: surface goal (settle the account) -> the settlement rule's three prerequisite sentences -> three states the records do not show -> three other policies' rules, each of which computes a figure of its own -> three writes -> only then the settlement figure, whose arrears, charge-share and credit components are all different once those writes have landed. The order cannot be swapped: evaluating the settlement first gives 840.08, 1521.77 or 2510.56 depending on which write is missing, and 2388.71 if the agent reads only the computation document.
Breadth: the settlement figure alone reads the instalment ledger, the payment ledger, the charge ledger split by kind, the credit ledger split by reason, the booking and completion ledgers, the term's entitlement credit, the term start day, the signature day and two tier parameters. Across the four computations the call also reads the demand service account's twelve-month invoice and payment history, its completed calls over six months, its prepaid hour balance and its status — a second product's records that no part of the caller's request mentions.

EASY MISTAKES, AND HOW THE POLICY EXCLUDES THEM
Taking the displayed balance_due of 2625.00 as the answer: the settlement rule states what the figure is built from and none of it is that field. Using the whole arrears (2275.00) instead of the four-month window: the arrears rule keys the window to the billing cycle, and this tier is billed in four instalments a year. Counting two months of arrears: the unattended-month relief rule takes whole completed months where one booked preventive visit stands unanswered. Dividing the annual price by the 8 visits the term credited when computing the credit: the divisor rule prefers the visits booked where they stand above the credited ones, and 12 do. Treating the no-access visit as consuming an entitlement visit: base says it consumes none, which is why ten visits and not eleven are consumed and why exactly two stand beyond the entitlement. Crediting WO-4180395 again: it already carries a credit. Billing WO-4182166 again: it already carries a charge of that kind; billing WO-4181921 or WO-4181455: in completion order they are the seventh and eighth consuming completions and sit inside the eight the term credited. Taking the square-account rate of 1.0 percent because the demand service account is clean: the rate ladder also asks whether the arrears exceed one instalment, and 2275.00 does.

STANDARD SOLUTION
Find the account, verify, read the agreement, read its whole history, read the intake records, read the owner's demand service program and its ledger. Compute and book the charge for instalments left unpaid against INV-40232744 (32.19). Compute and issue the credit for WO-4181288 against INV-40232744 (969.48). Compute and bill the additional visit WO-4182301 against INV-40232744 (701.00). Then compute the settlement figure on the world those three writes leave (1541.08), unlock the owner's own payment action, hand it over, and let her pay it by bank transfer against INV-40231188, the oldest unpaid invoice.

Every one of those figures is what computations[] carries, and the four results are exactly the four gold arguments.

FORWARD AND REVERSE SWEEP, rule <-> compute_basis <-> compute
Forward: every binding that reads the world, aggregates, branches, caps or rounds carries a verbatim quotation of the rule sentence that legislates it — checked mechanically by re-reading each compute_basis value out of the policy's own rule after whitespace normalisation, for all four policies, with no misses. Sensitive-word cross-check: quotations saying "in the last four months" / "in the last two months" / "over the last twelve months" / "in the last six months" sit on expressions carrying within_months=4, 2, 12 and 6; "taken at the ... share" sits on a multiplication by a K constant; "rounded to the nearest cent once, on the final result alone" sits on the single RND at the result; "never falls below nothing" sits on MX(0, ...).
Reverse: reading each rule through, every load-bearing sentence is claimed. The four opening sentences of each policy are its baseline paragraph and are claimed by the plain bindings and the result; every ladder sentence is claimed by its factor's decides binding; the three prerequisite sentences of the settlement rule are claimed not by compute but by the three declared edges, which is where they belong. No sentence promises a window, filter, branch, cap or rounding that compute does not implement, and no expression carries a filter the rule does not state.

SOLVABILITY EVIDENCE AGAINST GOLD
Each of the four call steps carries a contract entry. Steps 8, 10 and 12 are state_due and cite pre-action initial_state rows as their intent source, never the caller; step 14 is on_request and cites the caller's own words verbatim, with the discriminator phrase "she will make the payment in person on this call rather than have anyone do it for her" occurring verbatim in the cited snippet. Every base policy governing each write subject appears in base_preconditions, with policy_scope where base carries no gate on that subject and the full evidence-binding chain where it does (the missed-visit grace gate, correlated by work_order_ref to the action's work_order_ref argument). Stage provenance: the two charges and the credit are performed_by_this_tool or, for the additional visit, preexisting_before_conversation (the visit was completed 2026-08-12, before the call — the office is billing work already done, not booking work to come); the payment is established_by_prior_tool and cites prior_step 8, 10 and 12. Nothing in this task turns a status registration into a real-world event: no diagnosis, no visit, no clearing, no approval and no future date stands between the opening and the terminal state, and every one of the four writes lands synchronously under the single frozen_time of 2026-09-17 09:40:00 CDT.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT ALONE
Setting the extended yaml, compute, expected and gold aside and working only from what a rollout can see — the policy prose as it will be published, the tool schemas, the rows the share finders return and the caller's actual lines — the reading is: the caller wants a settlement; the settlement rule says the figure waits on three states; the finders show none of the three holds; the three other rules each compute their own figure from records the finders return; the four writes therefore run charge, credit, additional visit, settlement, and the parameters are forced at every step (the charges and the credit attach to the one instalment still standing, the work orders are the only unanswered booking and the one unbilled completion beyond the entitlement, the settlement lands on the oldest unpaid invoice as the base billing rule directs, and the payment channel is the one the caller names). Recomputing the four amounts by hand off the visible rows gives 32.19, 969.48, 701.00 and 1541.08 — the same as gold, with no second reading available at any step.


ROUND 2 REWORK — AUDIT ITEMS AND WHAT CHANGED (audits/policy_task/maintenance_agreement_desk, first revision)
- G-1 / F-0-1 (P1 "stands unsettled" had no stated counting convention): the dunning-rate ladder no longer counts instalments at all. Its second condition is now an explicit amount comparison stated in the rule — whether the instalments invoiced on the agreement exceed the payments received on it by more than the value of one instalment of the annual price in force — implemented as SUM minus SUM against annual price over instalment count. On this world 2275.00 exceeds 1775.00, so the customer sits on the repeatedly-run-behind tier at 1.25 percent; the part-paid Q1 invoice needs no row-versus-amount convention to be read, and the base measure's amount reading and the rule now agree. The charge moved from 27.75 to 32.19 and every downstream figure with it.
- G-2 / F-0-2 (a no-access closure counted as a completed visit): the settlement rule now says outright, in the write-down paragraph and quoted for performed_visits, that a booking the office attended and closed as a no-access call is taken as answered for this purpose, since the office attended, and does not count as a visit the office never performed; compute is unchanged and the two readings collapse to one (one unanswered booking, 443.75 written off). The same convention is stated in the reinstatement policy for lost visits, and the renewal policy now excludes no-access closures from the visits completed, as base's consumption sentence requires.
- F-0-3 (object of the additional visit charge not unique; GT identified the wrong visit): the world was reseeded so that the existing additional-visit charge sits on WO-4182166, the ninth consuming completion, and the unbilled beyond-entitlement visit is WO-4182301, which is also the most recent completion on the agreement (now a preventive visit of 5.5 hours outside regular hours; WO-4181921 became a 3.5-hour regular-hours preventive visit with a report). The policy's rule gained an object sentence fixing the visits beyond the entitlement by completion order with no-access consuming none, and naming the visit priced as the most recent visit completed on the agreement; its hours and band ladders now read the most recent completion of any kind (O-9 closed with it). user_scenario:
Dana Ferris keeps the books for Brightwater Property Group, LLC, a suburban landlord with three office parks and a payables calendar she guards jealously. She is brisk and a little dry, works from her own spreadsheet rather than from memory, and has rung the Halvorsen client services desk because she is closing the third quarter this week and wants the maintenance agreement on the Ridgeline Commerce Center settled up before she locks the ledger.

What she wants is plain enough: the desk is to work out what that agreement actually owes today and then read her the settlement figure so she can pay it herself there and then. So she says outright that she wants to settle the account on the Ridgeline maintenance agreement today, not have a number to think about over the weekend — she has the bank portal open, she is authorising the desk to put whatever the account needs through on their side, and she will make the payment in person on this call rather than have anyone do it for her. She wants it done today, on the Ridgeline agreement only; the other two buildings are on separate paperwork and she is not touching them.

She gives her name and the company at the start, and when the agent needs something to find the account with she reads out the number the office rings her on, 3125550137, for Brightwater Property Group, LLC. Asked to prove who she is before anything is touched, she reads the account number off the top of the last invoice, 610418, and gives the last four digits of the company's federal tax number, 1147. She has the billing address and the billing email somewhere in the file and will dig them out if the agent says two details are not enough, but she would rather not.

Everything else she gives only when she is asked for it. Which building: the Ridgeline Commerce Center, out on Ridgeline Parkway in Elmhurst. The purchase order the invoices have to carry: BW-2026-PM-118. How the money will move: a bank transfer pushed from the operating account, which is how she pays everything. Internal reference numbers she simply does not have — she tells the agent the office will have to read those off their own records, and she is not going to guess at one. If she is asked whether anything is in dispute she says no, she just wants it squared away.

She does have her own running figure in front of her, and if the agent reads her a settlement figure that is nowhere near it she says her spreadsheet has the Ridgeline balance sitting at about twenty-six hundred and asks them to put it against the record again before she pays anything. She will not say what the figure ought to be, because she does not know how the agreement prices any of it; she only knows what she has posted.

When the agent has the figure and hands her the means to pay it, she pays it — that amount, by bank transfer — and she reads back the confirmation reference the payment gives her so the agent has it on the call. Once she has that reference she says that is the quarter closed on Ridgeline, thanks them for sorting it out, and rings off.

The visit priced is the most recent visit completed on the agreement, WO-4182301 on 2026-09-09, which logged 5.5 hours against the 3.0 hours the additional visit price covers, an overrun of 2.5 hours; the owner holds a demand service rate program standing in active status, so the tier's agreement labor rate of 128.00 less the tier's repair labor discount of 15 percent is charged for each of those hours: 128.00 x 2.5 x 0.85 = 272.00. That visit was worked in the band outside regular hours and this tier carries no after-hours cover, so the unit price is raised by the tier's overtime multiplier of 1.5 acting on it: 306.00 x 0.5 = 153.00. The owner's prepaid technician hours stand at 4.5, at or below the block threshold of 8 and above none, so the part block reduction of 30.00 is earned. 306.00 + 272.00 + 153.00 - 30.00, rounded once at the end, is 701.00.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.invoice_ref: INV-40231188. Basis: the tool's own contract states this is 'the invoice number the payment is applied to, written as INV- followed by 8 digits, copied from an instalment entry in the agreement's history', and the base charter's billing rule, which the settlement policy leaves in force, states 'Payments are applied to the oldest unpaid invoice first, then to ancillary fees in the order they were charged; a customer may direct a payment to a named invoice instead, and where they do, that direction governs.' Uniqueness: the caller directs the payment to no invoice (she says the office will have to read reference numbers off its own records), so the oldest unpaid invoice governs; the 2026-Q1 instalment INV-40231188 of 1775.00 carries a payment of only 1275.00 against it and is the oldest instalment invoice standing unpaid, the 2026-Q2 instalment being paid in full and the 2026-Q3 instalment falling due later; no other invoice is the oldest unpaid one.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.settlement_amount_usd: 1541.08. The instalment arrears are written down for the visit the office never performed: instalments invoiced 5325.00 less payments received 3050.00 is 2275.00; twelve bookings stand against eleven completions, the no-access closure WO-4181690 being taken as answered because the office attended, so exactly one booked visit stands with no visit completed against it and half the value of a visit, taken as the annual price 7100.00 divided by the 8 visits the term credited, that is 443.75, is written off, leaving 1831.25. Two charges for instalments left unpaid now stand on the agreement (the 65.00 already there and the 32.19 booked on this call), so they are collected at the second notice share of 0.6: 97.19 x 0.6 = 58.31. The other ancillary charges standing are the 340.00 already billed for the earlier visit beyond the entitlement, the 125.00 short notice reschedule charge and the 701.00 billed on this call, together 1166.00. Exactly one visit was closed as no-access and no charge for a no-access trip stands on the agreement, so the tier's no-access trip fee of 145.00 is recovered. The credits issued on the agreement are set against the figure in full: the 180.00 already there and the 969.48 issued on this call, together 1149.48. The agreement carries two payments received and eight whole months of its term have run, more than six, so the established prompt allowance of 60.00 is allowed. The agreement was signed 2025-12-18, eight whole months before today and so no more than twelve, and no credit has been issued on it as a billing adjustment, so the tier's pre-agreement inspection fee of 450.00 is owed at the recent inspection share of 1.0. 1831.25 + 58.31 + 1166.00 + 145.00 - 1149.48 - 60.00 - 450.00, rounded once at the end, is 1541.08.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The three prerequisite problems hang in parallel off the root and none of them reads what another writes: the charge for instalments left unpaid reads the instalment and payment ledger, the count of charges of its own kind, the booked and completed preventive visits, the preventive reports and the demand service ledger; the credit reads the entitlement credit, the booked visits, the credits already issued for an unperformed visit, the term start day, the demand service calls and the short notice reschedule charges; the additional visit charge reads the charges of its own kind, the latest completion's hours and band, and the demand service program. A charge of one kind is invisible to a ladder that counts charges of another kind, and neither charge is a credit, so the three writes commute. Running them in the order late charge, credit, additional visit and again in the order additional visit, credit, late charge was checked against the verification script and produced the identical three amounts 32.19, 969.48 and 701.00 and the identical settlement figure of 1541.08, so the terminal state is the same whichever order is taken.

Skipping the credit for the unperformed visit leaves the settlement figure at 2510.56 instead of 1541.08: the credits set against the figure fall from 1149.48 to 180.00.
Skipping the additional visit charge leaves the settlement figure at 840.08 instead of 1541.08: the other ancillary charges fall from 1166.00 to 465.00.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: The persona never names a charge for instalments left unpaid, a credit for an unperformed visit or a charge for a visit beyond the entitlement, and never suggests that anything has to be sorted out first. All it carries is the surface goal — have the desk work out what the agreement owes and read her the figure so she can pay it — plus the general authorisation for the desk to put through whatever the account needs on their own side, which names nothing. Her only figure is the balance her own spreadsheet shows, about twenty-six hundred, which is the opening balance_due of 2625.00 on the agreement record and points at none of the three prerequisites.
